mi-msu-trustee-2026-lapietra-john.name: John Anthony La Pietra
mi-msu-trustee-2026-lapietra-john.bio: Attorney with prior experience in state, regional, and local government and in the private sector.

mi-supreme-court-2026-cavanagh-megan.name: Megan Kathleen Cavanagh
mi-supreme-court-2026-cavanagh-megan.bio: Michigan Supreme Court justice elected in 2018; former appellate lawyer in Detroit for more than 15 years.

mi-supreme-court-2026-hood-noah.name: Noah P. Hood
mi-supreme-court-2026-hood-noah.bio: Michigan Supreme Court justice; former Michigan Court of Appeals judge, Third Judicial Circuit Court judge, and federal prosecutor.

mi-supreme-court-2026-morse-bills-casand.name: Casandra Morse-Bills
mi-supreme-court-2026-morse-bills-casand.bio: Presiding Judge of Michigan's 23rd Judicial Circuit since 2018; former Oscoda County Prosecuting Attorney.

positions.stance: "A judge's job is to apply the law as it is written, not to reshape it according to personal preference."
"The courtroom is a place for interpretation, not legislation"; says honoring the boundary between making and applying laws upholds self-government.
Says judges must stand as a check against government overreach, guided by the plain text of the U.S. and Michigan Constitutions.
Believes everyone is entitled to the same standard of justice; "A judge's ruling should rest on two things only: the law and the facts."
Believes "disagreement does not require disrespect" and that litigants, attorneys, and judges deserve to be heard and treated with courtesy.

mi-supreme-court-2026-warren-michael.name: Michael Warren
mi-supreme-court-2026-warren-michael.bio: Oakland County Circuit Court judge for over two decades and business law professor at Wayne State University.

positions.stance: "Interprets the law as written — does not legislate from the bench."
Describes himself as "A steadfast originalist who interprets the law as written."
"Every decision rooted in a fair reading of the law — equal justice regardless of status, race, gender, or wealth."

wa-supreme-court-pos1-2026-melody-collee.name: Colleen Melody
wa-supreme-court-pos1-2026-melody-collee.bio: Washington Supreme Court justice; former first Chief of the Civil Rights Division in the Washington State Attorney General's Office and former U.S. Department of Justice attorney.

positions.stance: Believes courts must safeguard Washington's independence and "longstanding protection of rights in the workplace, in healthcare, and other individual civil and constitutional rights."
Believes everyone deserves to be free from violence, harassment, or discrimination, and that crime and discrimination victims "deserve dignity, respect, and safety."
"Our Courts are a cornerstone of our democracy and must be trusted and accessible to everyone."
"Judges are public servants. They must work hard, listen, and approach each case with impartiality and humility."

wa-supreme-court-pos1-2026-edwards-scott.name: Scott Edwards
wa-supreme-court-pos1-2026-edwards-scott.bio: Partner at Ballard Spahr in Seattle and adjunct professor of state and local tax at the University of Washington School of Law.

positions.stance: "Decisions guided by the law and the record — never by politics or pressure."
"Clear, principled reasoning that strengthens confidence in our courts."
"Respectful process, equal treatment, and an unwavering commitment to due process."

wa-supreme-court-pos3-2026-stevens-david.name: David Stevens
wa-supreme-court-pos3-2026-stevens-david.bio: Mason County Superior Court judge and Navy veteran; former prosecutor, tribal chief public defender, and HUD civil rights investigator.

positions.stance: Says the current court "believes that judges should evaluate the selection of jurors based on Race. I believe that is wrong."
Disagrees with limits the current court placed on trial judges issuing warrants when defendants miss court, saying courtroom experience matters "when liberty and public safety are at stake."
Believes the Washington Constitution "should be interpreted based on its text and original meaning and not on evolving societal standards."
"The Supreme Court is a constitutional court, not a policy-making body."
Says the court's role is "to interpret and apply the law as written and not on evolving societal standards or ideology."

wa-supreme-court-pos3-2026-hawk-jaime.name: Jaime Michelle Hawk
wa-supreme-court-pos3-2026-hawk-jaime.bio: King County Superior Court judge; former ACLU of Washington attorney and state and federal public defender.

positions.stance: Believes individual rights and equal protection "are not abstract concepts. They are what courts exist to defend."

wa-supreme-court-pos4-2026-birk-ian.name: Ian Birk
wa-supreme-court-pos4-2026-birk-ian.bio: Judge on Division I of the Washington State Court of Appeals since 2022; former partner at Keller Rohrback LLP and Washington Supreme Court law clerk.

positions.stance: Believes judges "must decide cases based on the law and the facts—never politics, pressure, or popularity."
"The justice system must work for everyone, not just those with resources or power"; calls equal access "foundational to equal justice."
Committed to careful attention to the record, respect for legal precedent, applying the law evenly, and explaining judicial decisions clearly.
Believes judicial decision-making "must be transparent, principled, and accountable to the law itself."
Approaches judging "with care, humility, and respect for the human consequences of the Court's work."

wa-supreme-court-pos4-2026-odonnell-sean.name: Sean O'Donnell
wa-supreme-court-pos4-2026-odonnell-sean.bio: King County Superior Court judge since 2013; former King County senior deputy prosecutor for 12 years.

positions.stance: Says his judicial philosophy is rooted in "compassion, fairness, independence, and honesty," and that faithful interpretation includes appreciating the law's effect on people and communities.
"I begin with the Constitution, the laws enacted by the Legislature, and the legal precedent that guides the Court in resolving cases and controversies."
"I believe that judges can honor victims' rights while vigorously protecting defendants' constitutional guarantees."

wa-supreme-court-pos5-2026-angelis-theo.name: Theo Angelis
wa-supreme-court-pos5-2026-angelis-theo.bio: Washington Supreme Court justice appointed in March 2026; former appellate and complex-litigation lawyer with more than 25 years of experience.

positions.stance: Believes the Court's foremost responsibility is "to faithfully interpret and apply the Constitution and laws of Washington State."
"Courts must remain independent and impartial"; committed to careful legal analysis and thoughtful decision-making.
Believes "the courts must remain open, accessible, and fair to all people."
Says the Supreme Court plays a critical role "in ensuring that Washington's laws are applied consistently and fairly."

wa-supreme-court-pos5-2026-larson-dave.name: Dave Larson
wa-supreme-court-pos5-2026-larson-dave.bio: Retired Federal Way Municipal Court judge with 18 years on the bench; former trial lawyer for 23 years.

positions.stance: Believes a justice should "not impose ideology" but ensure fair, dignified treatment and that "the law is applied as written, consistently, and without political pressure from any direction."
"Good judging isn't a worldview — it's a discipline"; reserve judgment until the record closes and "Apply the law as written, not as you wish it had been."
